# Rafiq v0.5.16: every command, boxed in

## New
- **A sandbox for commands.** Settings → Permissions → Command sandbox, enforced by the operating system rather than by the model:
  - **Contained** (the default): a command and everything it starts are one tree. When it times out or you stop the task, all of it closes, not just the first command.
  - **Strict:** a command can write only inside the working folder and a temp folder of its own. Any write anywhere else is refused by the system, whatever the command tries. On Windows it runs at Low integrity, with no clipboard, no shutdown, and limits on processes and memory; on macOS it runs under `sandbox-exec`.
- **Commands without the permission card.** With the strict sandbox on, you can let commands run on their own. A command set to «Deny» stays denied, and writes through the file tools still ask.

## Good to know
- The first time a strict command runs in a folder on Windows, Rafiq marks that folder (Low integrity) so commands may write there. Nothing above it is touched.
- Commands still read files and reach the network under the strict sandbox.

## Updating
Rafiq offers the update by itself. Or download `Rafiq_0.5.16_x64-setup.exe` below and check it:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\Rafiq_0.5.16_x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

Compare the result with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

macOS (Apple Silicon): [Rafiq-macos-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/AhmadALSaffan/RAFIQ/releases/download/macos/Rafiq-macos-arm64.dmg).
